title: POC weekly sync - onboarding & env readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync covering onboarding progress, infra access, initial perf results, tuning suggestions (batching/quant), and next steps for security docs and benchmark run.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-20
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Sarah (CTO - Veridian), Raj (ML Eng), Tom (DevOps)

Summary (auto): quick sync on pilot readiness and first perf pass, some infra kinks, agreed on next steps to run full benchmark and share security pack.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:05 Sarah: Sarah here.
00:07 Raj: Raj on the line.
00:09 Tom: Tom here.
00:12 Maya: great. Daniel, you want to kick off with the perf notes?
00:15 Daniel: yeah sure. so last week we ran the initial inference runs against the veridian test set, 10k requests, mixed lengths. overall latency p50 was around 120ms hosted, p95 about 480ms. throughput at about 65 rps on your 4-GPU machine when pinned to dedicated. note: some of the logs show kv cache misses because prefix caching wasn't wired up in your staging env.
00:42 Raj: when you say hosted vs dedicated, is hosted the redwood managed api? because we were expecting dedicated to be faster, we saw the reverse in one run.
00:50 Daniel: yep hosted means redwood managed; the anomalous run was because your node had background jobs and we hit swapping, so dedicated mode when isolated was better, the noisy neighbor caused the hosted run to show lower p50 sometimes. also quant profiles matter—when we used int8 quant we saw 1.8x throughput but some slight quality diffs on longer prompts.
01:12 Tom: i can confirm the staging node had a cron backup at 2am -- we missed that. we'll spin up a clean node for next bench. also quick question on networking: we're deploying in our VPC, do we need special firewall rules for the private control plane?
01:26 Maya: good q. for Redwood Private we need egress to the control plane endpoints on ports 443, and we provide a list of CIDR ranges in the security pack. for a fully on-prem bundle there's an air-gapped option but that needs the full install artifact.
01:41 Sarah: SOC2 and audit logs—how are those surfaced? we need to provide audit trails for PHI processing.
01:48 Daniel: we support audit logs and you can ship logs to your cloud object store; also we integrate with KMS for envelope encryption. we'll share the SOC2 documentation and the audit log spec. note: some fields in the logs are tokenized for pii.
02:05 Raj: on the model side, we tried with the default redwood-curated-3b; curious about model variants for latency/cost tradeoffs.
02:13 Daniel: typically for conversational clinical summarization you can try the 3b with int8 quant for cost sensitive workloads; if latency is critical try 2b distilled or a trimmed context. we also have a split-routing policy where short requests go to a cheaper low-latency model and long ones hit the larger model. we'll propose a routing policy config.
02:35 Raj: does that require changes in our code to route?
02:38 Maya: no, routing is configured in the Redwood Console per route, you can set thresholds by token length or latency SLO. we can send a sample config.
02:45 Tom: access wise we still don't have the service account IAM role in our GCP project for the benchmark runner. i opened the ticket yesterday.
02:52 Maya: ok we'll pause the benchmark until that's resolved; can you confirm the ticket id?
02:55 Tom: TKT-4821.
02:57 Maya: got it, we'll track it.
03:00 Daniel: another note on tuning: batching helps a lot for throughput but can add tail latency; since you have mixed short/long prompts we recommend dynamic batching with a small max batch size (8-16) and a latency cap. also prefix caching of common prompts reduced p95 by ~20% in our tests.
03:25 Sarah: great. QA on quality: Raj, did you see any hallucinations or critical errors in the outputs at int8?
03:32 Raj: minor hallucinations on entity linking in one test, mostly on long discharge templates, tolerable but we'd like to run an eval sweep.
03:40 Daniel: okay we'll run a quality regression check with your prompt set and include ROUGE/BLEU and a small human sample.
03:48 Maya: let's talk schedule and next steps. ideally we run the full 100k request benchmark next week once IAM and the clean node are in place.
03:56 Tom: we'll have the node provisioned by monday, and I'll push the IAM role today.
04:00 Maya: perfect. i'll share the benchmark playbook and the exact infra checklist.
04:05 Sarah: on contract/ pricing, we need a ballpark for dedicated during pilot.
04:09 Maya: ballpark for pilot dedicated (4 GPUs) is $8k/mo + overage, but we'll send an actual SOW.
04:15 Sarah: ok.
04:20 Raj: one more technical: your note about 'kv cache misses' earlier, can you explain the cause?
04:25 Daniel: sure — in our runtime we keep KV cache per session for autoregressive workloads; in staging the session ids were not sticky so cache warmed less, causing repeated recompute and higher token-costs. we gave a patch to persist session ids in the runner.
04:42 Raj: thanks.
04:44 Maya: any blockers i missed?
04:46 Tom: none beyond the IAM and clean node.
04:49 Sarah: sounds good. we'll aim for the benchmark next tuesday.
04:52 Maya: ok final recap: maya to send security pack + SOC2 docs, daniel to run quality regression and updated perf run once infra ready, tom to provision node and IAM, sarah to review pricing and confirm pilot budget.
04:59 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-transcriptions (kv cache -> kv cash) observed; speaker labels mostly accurate.
next_steps: Maya: Share security pack (SOC2, audit log spec, CIDR list) by 2027-01-21
Daniel: Run quality regression on customer prompt set and send results by 2027-01-24
Tom: Provision clean staging node and confirm IAM role TKT-4821 by 2027-01-24
Maya: Send pilot SOW and pricing details by 2027-01-22
All: Schedule benchmark run for week of 2027-01-25 once infra validated
